name: planning
title: Planning — portfolio and roadmap management as a calibrated decision loop

knowledgeBase: base-deck-v2.1.md — slides 8 (the loop), 12 (horizon determinants), 17 (the five practices), appendices A3 and B3 (the filled templates)
provenance.note: Authored, not migrated. The loop, the absorption/security gate, the horizon framework and the four template field lists are taken from the knowledge base. The surrounding evidence — magnitudes, vendor statistics and citations — is deliberately not taken: the same critic pass that found the templates sound marked that material for heavy revision.

roles.note: The six portfolio roles are inferred from the six phases, not sourced. The source research carries a confirmed-gap marker on engineering-manager portfolio responsibility and calls it unwritten territory, and that gap sits exactly on the seam between this pack and the coding pack. The phases, the gate, the templates and the horizon framework are evidenced; the role boundaries below are a proposal to be revised after the first real portfolio has run through them. Two properties are NOT provisional and follow from the process rather than the role literature: the gate reviewer must be a different party from whoever ran deliver, and the gate verdict must be a named token rather than prose. This note covers the six files listed here only; agents/target-reviewer.md is part 9 content and is not provisional.

parameters.prompt: What is this organisation's constraint floor? high-floor: a long-lead physical or regulatory constraint binds — clearance-gated programmes, hardware, certification. near-zero-floor: build is near-free, releases are continuous, and competitive substitution is the fastest-moving constraint.
